html:
The Wichí are an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco, the hot dry plain shared by Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay. They live mainly in Salta, Formosa and Chaco provinces of Argentina; in Bolivia they are called Weenhayek. Spanish settlers called them Mataco.

They lived by fishing on the Pilcomayo and Bermejo rivers, gathering algarrobo pods and honey, hunting and small gardens, moving with the seasons. The Spanish hardly reached them; their lands were only taken in the late 1800s and early 1900s, when Argentine armies pushed into the Chaco and many Wichí went to work on sugar plantations. Today they are among Argentina's largest Indigenous peoples. Their neighbours include the Qom (Toba).
